notes.title: Map Switching
notes.content:
The game world is now broken into smaller maps. This was done to improve the game's frames per second. You can switch to a different map at the main menu. More maps will be added in the future.

When continuing as an existing dinosaur, the player starts at a random position on the map.

If the player tries to create a new dinosaur on a map that does not have a nest for that species, the map's default nest is chosen and temporarily turned into a nest for the player's chosen species.

All dinosaurs now smell for a longer duration before the smelling highlights disappear.

The 'Return To Nest' button is now the 'Get Unstuck' button. It now teleports the player to a random location on the map according to the player's dinosaur's natural environment.

Dinosaurs no longer get thirsty from regenerating health and stamina, it was causing dehydration more than desired.

notes.title: Biome-Specific Dinosaur Spawns
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Each species of dinosaur now only spawns in specific biomes. Each dinosaur can have different spawn rates per biome, Common, Uncommon, or Rare. This determines how often they are encountered.
[*] Increased the range at which all pack followers will follow and stop following their leader.
[*] Adjusted some dinosaurs' 'Dominance' value. Now herbivores are less dominant than an equal-sized carnivore. This means carnivores are more likely to attack herbivores.
[*] Aquatic dinosaur spawns have been increased from 500 to 800. With the addition of biome spawn rates this should provide more smaller dinosaurs for food in the ocean.
[*] Different music now plays in each biome.
[*] Our composer has finished another music track, one for the jungle biome. You can hear it randomly play in the jungle along with a placeholder music track.
[/list]

notes.title: Dinosaur Weight
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Reduced the game's R.A.M. usage from approximately 5.9gb down to approximately 4.9gb.

[*] All dinosaurs now have a weight.

[*] Changed how much meat dinosaurs have on their body. I based this on their weight.

[*] Brachiosaurus has increased in size. From a scale of 1.6 to 2.6. Their overhead health-bar's position has been adjusted.

[*] Archelon has increased in size. From a scale of 2 to 2.7. Their overhead health-bar's position has been adjusted.

[*] Triceratops has increased in size. From a scale of 2.2 to 3.2. Their overhead health-bar's position has been adjusted.

[*] Adjusted all dinosaurs' bite size to be based on their body weight. 1.8% for carnivores and 0.18% for herbivores.

[*] The amount of food on trees has increased to be twice as much as previously.

[*] Dinosaur growth point requirements has changed for all dinosaurs. It is now based on their weight.

[*] The rate at which dinosaurs gain growth points passively over time has changed. For hatchlings, they gain 1% of their required growth points every 6 seconds. For juveniles, they gain 1% of their required growth points every 60 seconds. For sub-adults, they gain 1% of their required growth points every 600 seconds. For adults, they gain 1% of their required growth points every 6000 seconds.

[*] The rate at which dinosaurs gain experience points from food has been adjusted to be based on their weight.

[*] The amount of food a dinosaur has to eat in order to not starve has been changed to be based on their weight.

[*] The amount water a dinosaur has to drink in order to not dehydrate has been changed to be based on their weight.

[*] The rate at which dinosaurs get hungry has been changed to every in-game hour, which is two and a half minutes.

[*] The rate at which dinosaurs get thirsty has been changed to every in-game hour, which is two and a half minutes.

[*] A different set of music now plays while the player is underwater. Included in this set is one new musical track made by Will Dodson!
[/list]

notes.title: CPU and GPU Performance Optimizations
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Changed the game's render distance to be three times its current value.  Now land and vegetation can be seen very far away.

[*] Adjusted the overhead health-bar offset of some aquatic dinosaurs.

[*] Adjusted the height offset of the camera to be based on a dinosaur's health-bar offset and height.  Also the closer you zoom in the less affected the camera is by the health-bar offset, so its more centered on the dinosaur.

[*] Corpses no longer turn into a pile of meat when half of their flesh remains.

[*] The CPU now uses around 35% less processing power to play the game.  The GPU uses around 50% less processing power to play the game.  As a result of these two improvements the game's frames per second has decreased.  I will be looking for solutions to this setback.

[*] The underwater effect for freshwater has been temporarily removed.

[*] Rain particle effects are now working!

[*] Grass throughout the biomes has been changed.
	
[*] Overhead health-bar render distance has been increased from 100 to 500.

[*] The terrain's textures have received a visual overhaul.  Also, terrain textures no longer appear extremely glossy in the sunlight.

[*] The amount of flesh a dinosaur's body contains has been increased.

[*] Player dinosaurs no longer stand when smelling if they were sitting or sleeping, they instead will smell or cancel smelling.

[*] Player dinosaurs can now cancel smelling during the smelling cooldown phase.
[/list]

notes.title: FPS Increase
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Made a game optimization that increased FPS by 10 to 30 FPS, it varies by location in the game.
[/list]

notes.title: Smelling
notes.content:
[list]
[*] The smelling system is back in working order! Its much the same as its always been, highlights are harder to tell what exactly it is you're smelling other than a general 'its a carnivore', 'its a plant', 'etc'.
[*] You can also cancel smelling and remove highlights from your screen by pressing the Smell key again.
[/list]

notes.title: Playable Meganeura
notes.content:
[h1]Update 0.6.78.10[/h1]
[list]
[*] The Meganeura is now playable!

[*] Adjusted the flying 'fall speed' of the aerial dinosaurs.

[*] The wait time between switching dinosaurs has been removed because map data is not being loaded during this time anymore.

[*] There are now lock icons on the dinosaur select screen user interface next to the name of the species. These icons are visible when a species is locked from play and they disappear when you've unlocked that species for play.

[*] 5 bugs spawn at nests other than the players nest, up from 2.

[*] The pachycephalosaurus nest in the coniferous forest is no longer hidden inside a tree.

[*] Herbivore AI can now form herds with other species of herbivores.

[*] Herbivore AI can now call for help from other species of herbivores.

[*] Carnivore and piscivore AI can only call for help from their own species.

[*] All dinosaurs have had their call range, sight range, nest range, and wander range increased.
[/list]

[h1]Update 0.6.78.9[/h1]
[list]
[*] The day and night cycle is now one hour long.

[*] Dinosaurs now have a light-source at all times so they can see their immediate area when its night-time.

[*] The ammonite nest had collision and it shouldn't have, causing newly hatched ammonite and any nearby dinosaurs to become stuck and unable to move.
[/list]

notes.title: Piscivores
notes.content:
[list]
[*] There is a new food type, 'Fish'. Raw fish looks like raw meat except its whitish-pink in color. If it spoils it looks blueish-grey.

[*] The following dinosaurs now have a flesh type of 'Fish': Ammonite, Anomalocaris, Cameroceras, Dunkleosteus, Helicoprion, Leedsichthys, Megalodon, Onchopristis, and Xenacanthus.

[*] The following dinosaurs now have a diet of fish: Ammonite, Anomalocaris, Cameroceras, Helicoprion, Leedsichthys, Onchopristis, and Xenacanthus.

[*] Piscivores can eat fish but not meat.

[*] Carnivores can eat fish and meat.

[*] A new type of food is available for aquatic carnivores and piscivores to eat, starfish and shells. These function as plants do, restoring health, recovering from injuries quicker, and providing growth points and experience points.
[/list]

notes.title: Sitting and Sleeping
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Sitting or sleeping can be done with the 'R' key.  If the player tries to perform any actions while sitting or sleeping their dinosaur will stand up.  Some dinosaurs can call while sitting.

[*] The Resting button will only show up on the user interface if your dinosaur species can sit or sleep.

[*] Dinosaurs cannot sit or sleep if they are swimming or flying.

[*] Dinosaur hunger and thirst rate decreases while sitting or sleeping.

[*] Dinosaurs restore twice as much health while sitting or sleeping.

[*] While sitting or sleeping dinosaurs take half of their bleed damage and recover from bleeding twice as fast.

[*] While sitting or sleeping dinosaurs take half of their food poisoning damage and recover from food poisoning twice as fast.

[*] The dinosaurs that can sit, call while sitting, and sleep are: Ankylosaurus, Argentinosaurus, Brachiosaurus, Gallimimus, Iguanodon, Kentrosaurus, Ouranosaurus, Parasaurolophus, Protoceratops, Stegosaurus, Styracosaurus, and Triceratops.

[*] The dinosaurs that can only sleep are: Baryonyx, Carnotaurus, Compsognathus, Dilophosaurus, Dimetrodon, Dimorphodon, Oviraptor, Pachycephalosaurus, Pteranodon, Quetzalcoatlus, Spinosaurus, Troodon, Tyrannosaurus, and Velociraptor.
[/list]

notes.title: Elder Dinosaurs
notes.content:
Once a dinosaur reaches the Adult growth stage it then starts progressing towards the Elder growth stage. Growing into an elder, a dinosaur will get 1.5x as large as it was as an adult, and 1.5x as powerful.

There is a new button on the gameplay escape menu. "Return To Nest", it will return your dinosaur to their original nest location.

[b]Changes[/b]:
[list]
[*] Rare plants can now be eaten from ten times more than previously. This was done to make finding one more rewarding for longer and so players may be more likely to seek them out over other plants.

[*] Uncommon plants can now be eaten from three times more than previously. This was done to make finding one more rewarding but not as rewarding as a rare plant.

[*] Herbivores can now form herds with other species of herbivores. Carnivores can still only form packs with their own species. One herd/pack member is added per call and it is the closest dinosaur to you that meets the criteria to join you.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]:
[list]
[*] All Dinosaurs' footstep audio is once again controlled with the "Footsteps" slider in the game options audio menu, some of them had been switched to the combat audio slider.

[*] Random dinosaur spawns may not have been randomized differently upon game startup. This should be resolved and each time you start up the game there should be a different set of randomized dinosaurs spawned across the island. (Other than the nest guardians that always spawn around nests)
[/list]

notes.title: Stat Enhancement Update
notes.content:
[b]Changes[/b]:
[list]
[*] Dinosaur stat point enhancements are now saved differently. All stat point enhancement progress will be reset. Going forward I shouldn't have to reset the stats anymore, or at least not until I add in more forms of character development.
[*] The dinosaur stat enhancement screen has received a visual overhaul. Hover your mouse over an icon to find out more details. The icons used to indicate what stat you're hovering over are placeholder graphics.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]:
[list]
[*] Fixed rainy weather sometimes crashing the game.
[/list]

notes.title: Eating Controls Update
notes.content:
[b]Changes[/b]:
[list]
[*] Eating can now be done continuously without having to keep pressing the 'Eat' key, just by holding down the key instead.

[*] Drinking can now be done continuously without having to keep pressing the 'Drink' key, just by holding down the key instead.

[*] Eating and Drinking is now done from the same key.  'E'.  Eating is prioritized over drinking.

[*] 5 times as much thirst is replenished from each drink of water.

[*] The eating animation no longer plays every time you press the eating button, it only plays if you can actually eat something in front of you.  This should help make it more clear what you can and can't eat.

[*] All carnivores' bite size has been increased to three times its normal value.  All herbivores' bite size has been increased to two times its normal value.  This makes food appear larger in a dinosaur's mouth.  This makes dinosaurs have to eat less in order to gain the same amount of growth points, restore the same amount of health, restore the same amount of hunger, and gain the same amount of experience points.

[*] To compensate for gaining experience points faster due to a larger bite size, the required amount of food needing to be eaten in order to gain experience points has increased.  I am also increasing the required experience points a little beyond this compensation because I felt that experience points were gained a little too quickly.

[*] Argentinosaurus' Idle animation has been slowed to 25% of its current speed.
[/list]

notes.title: Flying Controls Update
notes.content:
[list]
[*] Dinosaurs now gain experience points from eating.
[*] You must accumulate X% of your previous growth stage's required growth points in order to gain experience points equal to one fifth of the cost of one stat increase.
[*] You cannot gain experience points through eating as a hatchling.
[*] This also works when you are full grown.
[*] Now herbivores and scavengers (carnivores as well) have a way to advance their stats that doesn't involve killing.
[*] Carnivores require 7.5% growth points.
[*] Herbivores require 15% growth points.
[*] As with gaining growth points for normal growth some sources give more growth points and this also affects how much you need to eat in order to gain experience points.
[/list]

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Changes:
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[list]
[*] While flying, your dinosaur no longer automatically turns to face the direction the camera is facing. The dinosaur now only turns when a directional key is pressed on the keyboard (W, A, S, D).

[*] While flying, pressing the forward directional key no longer makes your dinosaur dive.

[*] While flying, pressing the 'S' key will no longer slow down your dinosaur.

[*] While flying upwards, your dinosaur will slow down.

[*] While flying downwards, your dinosaur will speed up.

[*] While flying, pressing and holding the left control key will slow your dinosaur down until it is hovering. Continue holding down the left control key to hover.

[*] While flying and hovering, the player can now attack, smell, call for help, join pack, and leave pack.

[*] While flying and hovering you can use the movement keys for fine hovering precision.

[*] While flying and hovering you can now flap your wings with the spacebar to gain altitude but not be propelled forward.

[*] While flying you can now gain a quick burst of speed if you aren't at maximum speed by holding the 'Left Shift' key and pressing 'Spacebar'. Also works while hovering.
[/list]

Bug Fixes:

[list]
[*] Fixed some glitches with the different flying animations.

notes.title: High Definition Rendering
notes.content:

[*] The game now uses Unity's High Definition Render Pipeline.

[*] The jungle's vegetation is now affected by wind.

[*] There are now game announcements on the main menu screen. These can be toggled on and off.

notes.title: Common, Uncommon, and Rare Edible Plants
notes.content:
There are now common, uncommon, and rare edible plants for herbivores. The rarer a plant is the more nutritious it is and the more growth points it gives. Each biome has its own edible plants. Each biome's plants are worth different amounts of growth points so it may be worth traveling to other biomes in order to grow faster.



[b]Performance[/b]:
[list]
[*] The load time when you've chosen a dinosaur at the main menu and are loading into the game has been removed.

[*] The noticeable load time during gameplay of new patches of grass loading into the area has been removed. There should no longer be any freezes during gameplay.
[/list]

notes.title: Various Changes
notes.content:
The player can now turn their dinosaur without moving by holding the control key and then pressing a movement key. This does not work while flying.

The player can now smell nests. Their own nest is highlighted in light pink and other nests are highlighted in dark pink. Aquatic dinosaurs cannot smell nests on land. Only aquatic and amphibious dinosaurs can smell nests underwater. Nests can be smelled ten times further away than other things can be smelled. Up to four nests can be smelled at once, depending on the age of the dinosaur.

The player's dinosaur now has an acceleration rate that is used while moving. They'll start moving slower and pick up speed over time. Each species can have its own acceleration rate.

Aquatic nests now appear as seaweed.



[b]Changes[/b]:
[list]
[*] Leedsichthys now has gills.

[*] The meadow biome has been changed to the prarie biome, and its grasses have changed.

[*] The ocean biome has changed slightly.

[*] The Archelon and Sarcosuchus now play their swimming and water-idle animations slower.
[/list]



[b]Balance Tuning[/b]:
[list]
[*] Dinosaur speed no longer increases linearly from hatchling size to adult size. Instead there are four speeds, one for hatchling, juvenile, sub-adult, and adult. This allows younger dinosaurs to be faster but not quite as fast as the adults. Now, most dinosaurs are much faster at younger stages.

[*] Dinosaur movement speed has received a tuning pass.

[*] Dinosaur turn speed has received a tuning pass.

[*] All flying dinosaurs have had their stamina doubled so they can fly longer.
[/list]

notes.title: Biomes Update
notes.content: There have been major updates to the appearances of the deciduous forests, coniferous forests, jungles, and meadows.  They now have bigger trees, denser vegetation,  and different grasses.  The appearances of beaches, badlands, and the ocean have changed to a lesser degree.  The updating of the biomes will be a periodic and ongoing process.

notes.title: Playable Aquatic Dinosaurs
notes.content:
The player can now play as 12 new aquatic dinosaurs.  The Ammonite, Anomalocaris, Cameroceras, Dunkleosteus, Elasmosaurus, Helicoprion, Ichthyosaurus, Leedsichthys, Megalodon, Mosasaurus, Onchopristis, and Xenacanthus.

[*] Reduced the cost of starting a new dinosaur at advanced growth stages.

[*] Dinosaurs are now worth more experience points when killed.  This should help players gain advancements more quickly.

[*] Dinosaur growth has been adjusted to not grow as much when smaller.  They'll be halfway grown when reaching the sub-adult stage, not 3/4ths of the way grown.

[*] Compsognathus' movement speed has been reduced.  It was a little challenging to control it while turning sometimes.

[list]

notes.title: New Dinosaurs, Camera Speed Increase, and Temporary FPS Increase
notes.content:
You should now start noticing 13 new dinosaur species roaming around the island.  The Argentinosaurus, Baryonyx, Carnotaurus, Dimorphodon, Gallimimus, Pachycephalosaurus, Iguanodon, Kentrosaurus, Ouranosaurus, Protoceratops, Quetzalcoatlus, Styracosaurus, and the Troodon. [list]

All of those dinosaurs did take a good amount of processing power to have them all roaming around the map, hunting and eating food, fighting other dinosaurs, etc.  In the very near future, when I finish making these 13 new dinosaur species playable, I'll work on optimizing the game's performance some more.
[/list]

notes.title: Update (Three New Upgradable Stats)
notes.content:
[b]There are now three new upgradable stats[/b].
[list]
[*] Stamina, for sprinting longer distances.
[*] Health regen, for passive health regeneration and health restored per bite eaten.
[*] Stamina regen, for sprinting more often.
[/list]

notes.title: Update (Changes and Bug Fixes)
notes.content:
[b]Changes[/b]:

[list]
[*] Sarcosuchus and archelon can now drink water.

[*] Your current health now increases along with your maximum health when spending experience on health upgrades.
[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]:

[list]
[*] The underwater camera effect is now working properly.

[*] Carrying both plants and meat is now working properly for the player.

[*] Fixed a glitch that had to do with pressing the forward key while flying and turning, you should not have turned from pressing the forward key in flight.

[*] Dinosaur AI is now able to attack their target from the proper distance.

[*] The player's herbivores are now able to eat plants from the proper distance.

[*] Fixed a glitch where dinosaurs were sometimes spawning with more health, stamina, and oxygen than their maximum.
[/list]

notes.title: Land Movement Controls Upgrade for Player
notes.content:
[list]
[*]The player can now walk, run, and sprint left, right, and backwards with the A, D, and S keys. Diagonal directions also work.

[*]The camera, if not moved by the player, will remain facing in the dinosaur's original forward direction. 

[*]When all movement keys are released the player's dinosaur will face its original forward direction.
[/list]

notes.title: Changes
notes.content:
Herbivores can now smell nearby edible plants and trees.



----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Changes:
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Compsognathus turn speed was reduced slightly. The compsognathus felt a little out of control when turning sometimes.

Most dinosaurs have had their movement speed increased.

Pteranodon and velociraptor movement speed has been slightly decreased.

Brachiosaurus's size has been increased.

Dinosaurs can smell much further now, approximately 4 times as far.

Dinosaur growth point requirements have been adjusted. I'm trying to find the right balance of not taking extremely long to grow older, still having to spend some time in each growth stage, and having a sense of character development. If your herbivores are not growing very much from eating, try migrating to a new biome to see if the plants there may be more nutritious. If your carnivores are not growing very much from eating, try eating a fresh kill instead of left over meat, and also try to find what species are more nutritious.

Brachiosaurus has had its overhead health-bar position adjusted because of its recent size increase.

Dinosaur smell functions slightly differently now.  Instead of the distance linearly scaling based on the size of your dinosaur, it now works in four different steps.  One step for each growth stage, each 1/4th of the max distance further than the last.  This way hatchling dinosaurs' smell works without having to grow for awhile first.

Smelled targets are now sorted based on distance from your dinosaur and the closest targets are given priority.



----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Bug Fixes:
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The camera's underwater effect should no longer sometimes be activating upon continuing a saved dinosaur's progress when not in water.

notes.title: Eating Changes
notes.content:
[b]Changes[/b]:
[list]
[*] The required amount of growth points in order to grow to the next growth stage has been changed.

[*] Ants now give twice as many growth points when eaten.  Spiders now give three times as many growth points when eaten.  Mantis now give four times as many growth points when eaten.

[*] All dinosaurs now give more growth points when eaten.

[*] All plants now give more growth points when eaten.

[*] Dinosaurs gain twice as many growth points when they're hungry.

[*] Carnivores gain twice as many growth points when they eat from a fresh corpse.  Does not work for insects.

[*] Herbivores gain twice as many growth points when they eat from a live plant.
[/list]

notes.title: Saved Dinosaur Progress
notes.content:
[list]
[*] The dinosaur selection screen has been recreated.

[*] The player's dinosaur progress is now saved so they can play that dinosaur during other play sessions and pick up where they left off.

[*] Once the player gets a species to grow to a new growth stage (juvenile, sub-adult, adult), that growth stage is unlocked permanently. Unlocked growth stages can be selected when creating a new dinosaur to advance to that stage from the beginning. Using this feature costs evolution points.

[*] Dinosaurs gain experience points when they reach a new growth stage.  Experience points can be used to gain damage, health, and speed bonuses.
[/list]



[b]Changes[/b]:

[list]
[*] A dinosaur can only have experience spent on increasing stats if they are alive.

[*] Dinosaur's no longer animate walking or running one time when they spawn.

[*] Tier 2 species cost 1,000 evolution points each to unlock permanently. Tier 3 species cost 2,500 evolution points each to unlock permanently. Tier 4 species cost 5,000 evolution points each to unlock permanently.

[*] Dinosaurs now take longer to grow because their progress is no longer lost after each session.

[*] Insects no longer spawn around hatchling and juvenile dinosaurs.

[*] Twice as many insects spawn around nests.
[/list]

[*] World Streamer 2 integration is being retired until Unity fixes two glitches in their engine. One, a lag spike occurs when loading new scenes. Two, system memory is not freed when unloading scenes. Scenes being the containers for each chunk of terrain, this was causing bad performance issues to occur. This change is reducing system memory usage dramatically for the time being and generating no lag spikes because no terrain needs to be loaded dynamically.
[/list]

notes.title: Map Remake
notes.content:
The game now features a new, better looking, and much larger map! This new map is approximately 256 times larger than the current in-game map. There should now be plenty of room for many more dinosaurs, more exploring, and for the future growth of the game.

The map features 6 different biomes which are all home to different dinosaur species. Beaches, meadows, deciduous forests, coniferous forests, jungles, and badlands.

The new map will be improved as development continues.

Random dinosaurs now spawn around the map when the game is started. These dinosaurs will roam the island until they die or the player resets the map. When one dinosaur is killed another one will take its place somewhere else.



[b]Improvements[/b]:
[list]
[*] Any dinosaur, regardless of age, can eat insects.
[*] Dinosaur AI older than a hatchling no longer try to eat insects unless starving.
[*] Insects now grow up to twice their previous size.
[*] Insects now have a 100% chance to spawn around the hatchling player every thirty seconds instead of a dinosaur spawning.
[*] Insects now have a 100% chance to spawn around the juvenile player every two minutes instead of a dinosaur spawning.
[*] Dinosaurs no longer randomly spawn around other dinosaurs.
[/list]

[*] There is now a 30 second delay before you can click the main menu's 'Singleplayer' button after hatching as a new dinosaur. This was necessary to reduce the amount of possible memory usage spikes when hatching as dinosaurs repeatedly in different locations.
[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.3.53.4

[b]Improvements[/b]:

The user interface is now overlaid with text that labels each of the icons and buttons so the player has an easier time figuring out how to play the game.  This overlay can be toggled on and off by pressing the 'F3' key.

Now when a random dinosaur spawns passively around another dinosaur it has a 5% chance to ambush and attack the dinosaur it spawned around, down from a 100% chance.  This should give the player the upper hand with random spawns and when they would like to engage them.
	
The player's passive random area dinosaur spawns happen every 15 seconds as a hatchling, every 30 seconds as a juvenile, every 45 seconds as a sub-adult, and every 60 seconds as an adult.  This should help the area around the player feel a little more active the longer the player stays in the area.

Now when a dinosaur spawns from another dinosaur making a call for help it has a 10% chance to ambush and attack the dinosaur it spawned around, down from a 100% chance.
	
The chance for AI to have a random dinosaur spawn around it when calling for help has been decreased from 10% to 5%.  This should help a little with some overcrowding issues when dinosaurs call for help a lot.

notes.title: Update 0.2.49.5
notes.content:
The game's input controls have been changed to be more in-line with other dinosaur games to make it easier to pick up and play.  I like these controls enough to leave them here unless I get enough feedback that something should be changed.  In the future I will enable the game options input tab and let the user change their key-bindings.  In-game instructions have been changed to reflect these new key-bindings.

'Escape' key : Opens and Closes the gameplay menu.
'Escape' key : Closes the instructions window.
'F1' key : Toggle overhead health-bars on/off for other dinosaurs.  (must be playing as a dinosaur and alive)
'F4' key : Toggle the user interface on/off.  (must be playing as a dinosaur and alive)

'WASD' keys : Move your dinosaur.
'BackQuote' key : Toggle between walking and running modes.
'Left Shift' key : Sprint.  (must be moving forward)
'Left Click' mouse : Perform a basic attack.
'Q' key : Smell for food and dinosaurs.
'E' key : Eat food.
'G' key : Pick up or drop food.
'F' key : Drink water.  (must be standing in or next to fresh water)

'1' key : Call for help.  (Sometimes alerts aggressive dinosaurs of your location)  (useful for luring in prey)

'2' key : Start a pack or herd.
(You must have grown older than a hatchling and your species must be one that travels in packs or herds)
(The current amount of pack or herd members is displayed on the Pack button as the first number)
(The maximum amount of pack or herd members is displayed on the Pack button as the second number)
(As your dinosaur grows older your maximum pack size may increase)

'3' key : Leave your pack or herd.

notes.title: Update 0.1.46.0
notes.content:
I started playing Isles of Pangaea this morning after I had enabled the evolution point cost for new dinosaurs and my dinosaurs just kept dying within the first few minutes of gameplay.  I thought maybe I should add an evolution point refund mechanic that refunds your evolution points when you die within five minutes of starting a new dinosaur.  Then I got to thinking you know what would be better than making the player grind for evolution points any time they wanted to play a more powerful dinosaur?  Giving the player a sense of accomplishment and allowing them to permanently unlock a dinosaur species with evolution points, then their dinosaurs dying often won't be such a burden.  So I give to you, Update 0.1.46.0 (The Unlocking), the new dinosaur species unlocking system!  Spend evolution points one time to unlock a species and then you can play that species as many times as you like without having to spend any more evolution points.  This new mechanic uses the new save data system so you won't lose your progress.
		
	Please let me know what you think about how much the species unlocks cost, is it too much, or not enough?  I wanted the higher tiers of species to require some time and effort to be spent in order to unlock them because they are more powerful.  Plus when multiplayer functionality goes live, if you see someone with a higher tier of dinosaur you'll know they survived a lot to earn it.
